proof: If $W_i=0$, the cap part $\alpha_0\mu_i$ has mass zero and $\alpha_0\Psi_i=0$. Otherwise the two probability means obtained by dividing by $W_i$ belong to $C$ by convexity and have the same real base. Their continuous difference belongs to $D_{\rm all}$. Its pairing with $u_i$ equals the difference of their margins, which by affinity is $\alpha_0\Psi_i/W_i$, because the section and contact terms lie on the cutting plane. Its pairing is at most $h_{D_{\rm all}}(u_i)=1$. The sum follows from $\sum_i\lambda_{zi}=1$.

statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be a compact convex body with positive-volume integer fibers and mixed volume $\mu$ on those fibers. Write $D_{\rm all}=\{v:(0,v)\in C-C\}$. Take a cap with affine margin $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$ and $h_{D_{\rm all}}(u_i)=1$. Let $\Psi_i=\int (L_i)_+\,d\mu$ and let $\mu_i=\mu|_{\{L_i\ge0\}}$ have mass $c_i$. Suppose a finite nonnegative section measure $\sigma_i$ on $C\cap\{L_i=0\}$ has mass $S_i$ and a finite nonnegative contact measure $\nu_i$ is also supported on $C\cap\{L_i=0\}$. If for $\alpha_0,r_i\ge0$ the measures $\alpha_0\mu_i+r_i\sigma_i$ and $\nu_i$ have common mass $W_i=\alpha_0c_i+r_i S_i$ and common base first moment, then $\alpha_0\Psi_i\le W_i$. In particular, in a normalized stress with $\alpha_0=1$ and contact masses $\sum_z\eta_z\lambda_{zi}$ for $\lambda_z\in\Delta_N$, this gives $\Psi_i\le c_i+r_iS_i$ and $\Psi_D\le\sum_z\eta_z$.
title: Same-real-base width bound from mass and base moments
